original_card.question: Can a changed query demand or caller remove real work while satisfying native chronology and restoration?
methods: Construct and independently check one source-bound instance of the stated first experiment.
Seek an exact counterexample or target-specific complete-budget obstruction to that same proposed change.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A source-bound arbitrary-input identity and legal producer/consumer boundary with the complete paid and productive target invoice, including restoration, ownership, native alignment and extra charges. Price under the actual current model; historical ceiling.py assumptions must be established before use. A favorable optimistic relaxation keeps a route open but is not a completed supplier. A scoped local result remains useful; expansion requires the family-level budget gate.

first_step.scope: Source-bound orientation only, not a supplier replay or theorem proof.

original_card.first_experiment: Choose an exact caller and a new demand/interface hypothesis. Read the scoped #5617/#5631/#5649/#5747 and #5720/#5745 objections before rebuilding an excluded schedule. Compare the complete matched source/consumer protocols including all retained helper outputs. For an active-mode injection, first check #5745: its canonical delivery claim repays the eight removed centre jobs. Audit that exact claim or change its channel/feedback hypothesis; do not repeat the same free-injection search. Stop if the full favorable budget fails or the required restored output is unobservable.

actual_scope: Per-port linear-information floor for the fifteen thin QUERY_SHEAR stages of the retained p16 controllers (PR5398 direct controller, joint-helper-lattice source, p104 productive all-forward controller): with the eighteen full calls kept, free scalar ADD/swap/even central powers/markers, and rank-one latent channels evaluated on one available content each, at least fifteen requests per port are needed; evaluates atlas kappa-0035 target P8 (528 requests in place of 15 x ports).
scope_change_reason: The card asks whether a changed query demand or caller removes real work. Atlas PR5586 target P8 proposes exactly such a changed demand for the thin query stages (a causal state-space realization with at most 528 requests). Before constructing one, the exact per-port information count shows that no realization in the stated linear model can use fewer than fifteen requests per port, i.e. fewer than the present count, so P8 cannot be instantiated without a channel that serves several ports at once.
bottleneck_link: The fifteen thin stages cost one rank-one request per port line (1,560 on the p104 word, 1,680 on the PR5398 controller), the only pool of paid rank-one work outside the local word; each removed request is worth about +4.1e-6 of conditional saving on the PR5907 word and the P8 plan (1,560 -> 528) would be worth about +0.0043. The floor shows the pool is incompressible per port: every shear result is linearly independent of the free span and of the other fourteen.
stop_rule: Stop when the floor is computed exactly on all three retained controllers for two central-square values, each result is shown independent of all others, the greedy causal realization attains the floor, and the three controls (redundant shear recognised free; contents-free model and odd-powers-free model collapse to 0) pass.

open_questions.question: Can one latent Gaussian channel serve several port lines at once inside the P104 physical contract (fixed central port and 17-axis route per port), so that the per-port floor does not bound the total request count?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It is the only way left for atlas target P8: with per-port channels the minimum is 15 x ports, the present count.
open_questions.first_step: State the cross-port channel as a physical job in research/p104-productive-controller/caller.py terms (which native map, which rank, which route allowance) and price it in the complete invoice; a channel of rank r serving k ports must cost less than k H1.
open_questions.blocked_by: A new physical primitive, not this package.

open_questions.question: Does the floor survive the symbolic stage markers D_s (not specialised) with the same value fifteen, or is it larger?
open_questions.why_it_matters: A larger symbolic floor would not change the conclusion; a smaller one is impossible because specialisation is a homomorphism. Only of interest for a sharper statement.
open_questions.first_step: Repeat portfloor.analyse over K(theta, D_0..D_33) with the markers as symbols; the module needs a field of rational functions instead of Fraction.
open_questions.blocked_by: Nothing; a few hours of work.
